context.title: The Righteous Branch
context.summary: God condemns the shepherds who scattered His flock and promises to gather it and raise up for David a righteous Branch called 'The Lord Our Righteousness.' The rest of the chapter attacks false prophets who speak dreams from their own hearts, promising peace, though God never sent them.
context.background: 'The Lord our Righteousness' (v. 6) is Yahweh tsidkenu in Hebrew, a pointed contrast with Judah's last king, Zedekiah, whose name means 'the Lord is righteous.' False prophets were a serious problem in Judah's last years (chapters 27–29), offering dreams and visions that told people what they wanted to hear.

customs.note: 'Burden' (massa) was a standard term for a prophetic message, but it also meant a heavy load. When people mockingly ask for the latest 'burden,' God replies that they are the burden He will cast off.

watchFor: Bad shepherds and the good Shepherd (vv. 1–4); compare Ezekiel 34.
'Am I a God at hand… and not a God afar off?' (v. 23).
God's word is like fire and like a hammer (v. 29).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Gomorrah
places.summary: Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim which were destroyed by fire (Gen. 10:19; 13:10; 19:24, 28). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
